edits.current: The separate [scalar entry-counter receipt](evidence/php-fin-dispatch-20261008/receipt.json) records ordinary-source and reviewed-IR native PHP Composer packages after source removal, offline installation and relocation. Rejected `mirror`, `impossible` and `label` calls entered neither the Lean source nor its C adapter. Valid calls, including those after rejected ones, entered their own source and adapter once. Both consumers passed 2,028 checks on PHP 8.2.33 with FFI on x86-64 Linux and a glibc 2.36 package floor. An `LD_PRELOAD` interposer counted the entries without changing the installed package. It covers these top-level scalar calls, not nested refinements, PHP-Wasm or other platforms.

The separate [scalar entry-counter receipt](../evidence/wit-fin-dispatch-20261008/receipt.json) records ordinary-source and reviewed-IR Wasmtime host packages after source removal, offline installation and relocation of their local libraries. Rejected `mirror`, `impossible` and `label` calls entered neither the Lean source nor its C adapter. Valid calls, including those after rejected ones, entered their own source and adapter once. Both consumers passed 2,027 checks with the Wasmtime 42.0.1 C API and wasm-tools 1.245.1 on x86-64 Linux and a glibc 2.36 package floor. An `LD_PRELOAD` interposer counted the entries without changing the installed host. It covers these top-level scalar calls, not record or variant fields, containers or other platforms.

edits.previous: A Lean `Fin n` parameter or result is a `java.math.BigInteger`, the same as `Nat`. For `Library.mirror (value : Fin 10) : Fin 10`, `mirror(BigInteger.valueOf(3))` returns 6. `mirror(BigInteger.TEN)` throws `IllegalArgumentException` with the message `arg0 is not below its Fin 10 bound`. `null` throws `NullPointerException`, and a negative value throws the `IllegalArgumentException` that `Nat` throws. The package checks the bound before it calls Lean, so caller data is unchanged and a later valid call still works. `Fin 0` parameters reject every value, and bounds wider than 64 bits are compared exactly. Javadoc on each method and the package README state the bound. Top-level parameters and results are supported, including inside `Array`, `List` and `Option` (for example `Array (Fin 10)` or `Option (List (Fin 10))`): every element is checked before Lean is called, an empty array or `none` is valid even for `Fin 0`, and a rejection names the parameter and the bound of the element that failed. Fields, callbacks, products and results are not; see the [installed checks](../evidence/native-fin-hosts-20261006.md) and the [container checks](../evidence/native-fin-containers-20261006.md).

The separate [scalar entry-counter receipt](../evidence/jvm-fin-dispatch-20261009/receipt.json) records ordinary-source and reviewed-IR JARs after source removal, offline installation and relocation, with Java and Kotlin callers in separate processes. Rejected `mirror`, `impossible` and `label` calls entered neither the Lean source nor its C adapter. Valid calls, including those after rejected ones, entered their own source and adapter once. Both Java consumers passed 2,023 checks on OpenJDK 22.0.2 with GDB 13.1 on x86-64 Linux and a glibc 2.36 package floor. GDB counted the entries in the one verified directory the JAR extracted, without changing the generated loader or the extracted files. It covers these top-level scalar calls, not containers, nested refinements or other platforms.
